title: Describe a time when you gave advice to others
content: Well, I'd like to talk about a time when I gave advice to others. It happened during my first internship when I was still a junior student. A junior classmate of mine came to me asking how to improve his professional skills. Before that, I had asked a similar question to one of my senior schoolmates. He sincerely gave me practical advice, and that really helped me get started. After that, I promised I would try my best to be just as kind and helpful as he was to me. So, when the junior reached out, I spent time helping him learn how to use GitHub effectively, which is a free and open-source platform widely used by programmers. To be honest, while guiding him, I sincerely felt the same warmth and sense of purpose that my senior had once given to me. I believe that's why helping others matters so much. In the future, I will keep offering advice whenever I can, and I hope one day my junior will do the same for someone else.

title: Hobbies - Basketball and Video Games
content: Do you have any hobbies? Yes, of course. I have a few hobbies. I like playing basketball and video games in my free time because they help me exercise and enjoy myself. In addition, it's my favorite way to relax. Have you had any hobbies since you were a child? Absolutely. I've loved playing computer games since I was a child. Every day after school or on the weekends, I couldn't wait to play even if I hadn't eaten dinner. Actually, I think that might be the reason why I majored in computer science later. When I was younger, I dreamed of becoming a game developer or programmer, and that early passion really shaped my career path.

title: Describe an occasion when you were not allowed to use your mobile phone
content: Well, I'd like to talk about a time when I was not allowed to use my mobile phone. It happened in my high school, where students were strictly prohibited from using their phones. We couldn't even bring them to school. This rule was introduced when I first entered high school. I'd never had the freedom to use my phone without my parents' restrictions, so the school policy didn't bother me much at first. The school made this decision because they found that students had lost their focus on studying due to excessive phone use. As it meant we had no access to our devices during school hours, we had to rely on face-to-face communication and physical textbooks instead. Looking back, I think this experience taught me a valuable lesson about not being overly dependent on technology.

title: Describe a foreign country you would like to stay - Japan
content: Well, I'd like to talk about a foreign country that I'd love to stay in for a short period of time, and that's Japan. I visited it a year ago, and I was genuinely impressed by how polite and warm Japanese society feels. Before that trip, I actually had quite a negative impression of Japan. I thought Japanese people were cold and distant. However, during my trip, I noticed a small but meaningful thing. People always said 'sumimasen,' which means 'sorry' in Japanese, whenever they accidentally bumped into someone or needed to pass by. That small gesture revealed their deep-rooted respect for personal space. I think staying there for a few months would allow me to experience this culture more deeply and perhaps pick up some of that politeness myself.

title: Describe a piece of technology - Apple Watch
content: Well, I'd love to talk about my dream piece of technology: the Apple Watch. It's been my favorite wearable device since I was a kid. When I was in primary school, I always felt really envious whenever my classmates showed off their Apple Watches in class. They talked about how advanced they were, and back then, I just dreamed of having one too. However, it's quite expensive, around 3000 Yuan, but generally, you get what you pay for. It has amazing health-monitoring features like heart rate tracking and sleep analysis. For many people, it's also become a status symbol that represents a modern lifestyle. I believe if I owned one, it would not only help me manage my health better but also motivate me to stay active throughout the day.

title: P3 Discussion - Movies and Cinema
content: What kinds of movies do you think are successful in your country? Well, from my perspective, I think science fiction films are quite successful in China. For instance, almost everyone in our country, and even many people around the world, have heard of The Wandering Earth. It has received a lot of positive reviews, and its third installment is scheduled for release next year. What are the factors that make a successful movie? I believe it's the thematic depth. A successful movie doesn't just entertain the audience; it also encourages them to think deeply about its underlying message and figure out what the director is really trying to say. Do Chinese people prefer to watch domestic movies or foreign movies? Personally, I think Chinese people prefer domestic movies. The main reason is that they find the stories more relatable and familiar, especially the cultural background and everyday life shown on screen. Compared with foreign movies such as those from Hollywood, viewers often encounter two key barriers: the language gap and the differences in cultural values.

title: Describe a natural place - Gaoshan Village
content: I'd like to talk about a natural place in my hometown, which is called Gaoshan Village. It is a famous mountain in my hometown, and I have been there many times. In the past, I usually went there with my family during the Spring Festival every year. We climbed this mountain as exercise and prayed for good luck at the temple. Gaoshan Village is not very high, only about 400 meters above sea level. However, it is the only tourist attraction in my hometown, so during vacations, there are always a lot of visitors. To be honest, I didn't understand the meaning of climbing mountains when I was young. I just regarded it as a task that I needed to finish and reach the top. However, when I grew up, I began to realize that the most important thing is not to finish the task, but to enjoy the scenery and the time with family during the climbing process. In the future, I will still visit this place with my family and treat it as a time when we can reunite and relax.

title: Describe a time when you received good service in a shop - Camera in Japan
content: I'd like to talk about a time when I received good service in a shop. It happened in a local electronics store when I wanted to buy a new camera during my trip to Japan. Before I went there, I had prepared to spend a lot of time finding the camera I wanted. I also used my phone to look for a practical online guide. However, when I saw the wide variety of digital products on display, I was completely overwhelmed. It was so amazing because I had never seen so many digital products in one place. While I was still confused, a shopping assistant asked me whether I needed help. I sincerely nodded and used a translation app to tell him the specific camera model and features I was looking for. With his help, I finally bought my favorite camera within 10 minutes. To be honest, I really appreciated the professional service that the assistant provided. It actually saved me a lot of time on my trip. In the future, if I travel to Japan again, I will definitely visit this shop because its great service left a deep impression on me.

title: P1 Discussion - Food and Hakka Cuisine
content: What is your favorite food? Well, if I had to pick one, I'd say my favorite food is Hakka stuffed tofu. It is a special local dish in the Hakka region. People consider the tofu to be a traditional staple, and it's filled with a savory meat mixture. Why do I love it so much? Because I could hardly find the same taste anywhere else after I left my hometown. As a result, every time I see this dish, it makes me feel homesick. What kind of food did you like when you were young? In my memory, I loved junk food when I was young. Even though it was called junk food, I regarded it as a reward for my hard work. What I mean is, every time I did a good job or got an excellent score on an exam, my mother would always take me to fast food restaurants such as McDonald's or KFC for a feast. I loved it very much. Do you eat different foods at different times of the year? Absolutely. At home, my mother grows vegetables and raises animals by herself. So I can eat different foods at different times of the year, including various seasonal vegetables. What's more, I sometimes eat special foods like mooncakes or tangyuan during festivals such as the Mid-Autumn Festival and the Lantern Festival. Has your favorite food changed since you were a child? Of course. My favorite food changed to Hakka fermented glutinous rice wine when I became an adult and left home. It is a traditional Hakka drink made from glutinous rice, natural yeast, and spring water. For me, it reminds me of my family and brings back a lot of warm memories.

title: P1 Discussion - Sports Team and Basketball
content: Have you ever been part of a sports team? Absolutely. I was part of a sports team in high school. I was a key player on my class basketball team, serving as the point guard. As the name suggests, it is a position where you need to control the ball and organize the attack. Are team sports popular in your country? Yes, they are quite popular in my country. Team sports such as football, basketball, and tennis are great ways to demonstrate our cultural values of cooperation and mutual support. In addition, these sports have their own professional leagues in China, such as the CBA and CSL. Do you like watching team games? Why? To be honest, I hardly watch team games because I think it's more interesting to participate rather than just watch. I tend to enjoy playing the game myself rather than spending time watching broadcasts. What are the differences between team sports and individual sports? Well, from my perspective, the biggest difference is team collaboration. Obviously, team sports not only require personal performance but also demand team cooperation. In contrast, individual sports only require the former.

title: Describe your perfect job - Tencent Internship
content: Well, in my experience, my perfect job was an internship at Tencent. It was a typical 9-to-5 office job, which aligned well with my lifestyle. Before I got this internship, I never thought I could find a job that suited my major, Computer Science, so well. Every time I encountered a difficult coding problem on my own, I had to spend more than an hour figuring it out with no one to help me. In contrast, when I had trouble with my work at Tencent, my colleagues always helped me carefully and patiently. To be honest, this internship not only improved my professional skills but also changed my understanding of what a good job is. Before that, I used to think people in the workplace kept to themselves, but my colleagues changed that perception. They turned the workplace into a warm, interactive community, making the work feel enjoyable rather than stressful. If I have the chance to choose a job in the future, I will undoubtedly choose one similar to my Tencent internship because it set a perfect standard for my ideal job.

title: Describe a story you read recently - AI replacing programmers
content: Well, I'd like to talk about a story I recently read. It was about how artificial intelligence might replace programmers by 2028. I first came across AI when I was a freshman, about three years ago. To be honest, I never thought it would become as capable as human programmers in the coding field. Most of us just regarded it as a toy tool. However, with the rapid development of technology, the capabilities of AI have improved dramatically. The story says that AI tools, such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, have transformed from simple chatbots into smart assistants, particularly in computer science. From my perspective, I think it's both exciting and unsettling. As a programmer, I use AI tools in my daily work. What this means is that AI already has strong professional skills; it just needs a person to guide it on how to work. In the future, I believe that AI will be able to complete the work entirely by itself. At that point, the story might actually come true.

title: P3 Discussion - Vehicles and Environment
content: Which form of vehicle is more popular in your country: bikes, cars, or motorcycles? Well, from my perspective, I think cars are the most popular in our country, especially in Shenzhen, which is a fast-paced city. Every day when I commute to work or head back home, there are a lot of cars on the road, and we call it morning rush hour and evening rush hour. In contrast, bikes and motorcycles are often used for short, flexible trips. Do you think air pollution comes mostly from vehicles? No, I don't think so. To be honest, with the development of green energy, modern vehicles are becoming much cleaner compared to other sources of pollution, such as heavy industries or air travel. Although current vehicles still produce some emissions, they are definitely not the main source of air pollution. Do you think people need to drastically change their way of transportation to protect the environment? Absolutely not. I believe that would be an unnecessary step, as every form of transportation has its special function and plays a complementary role. If we want to protect the environment, it would be better to make small but meaningful changes, such as choosing electric vehicles or taking the metro for daily commutes.

title: P3 Discussion - Leisure Time in China
content: Do people like to spend their leisure time outdoors in your country? Of course. China has a lot of tourist attractions, and local governments invest in tourism significantly. As a result, more and more people are drawn to explore different places during their leisure time, including both domestic and international tourists. How do people spend their leisure time in your country? Well, people in our country generally play sports with their friends or children in their free time. Take my city, Shenzhen, as an example. There are a lot of posters encouraging people to exercise more, and the government has built many parks in local communities over the past 10 years. So it has become quite common for locals to go jogging or play basketball in their free time. How does technology affect the way people spend their leisure time? Well, technology, especially social media, has significantly influenced people's leisure habits. Thanks to platforms like TikTok, people can easily access the latest content through the Internet, and many follow lifestyle suggestions from celebrity influencers. As a result, things like short video challenges and live-streamed activities have become popular ways to spend free time, sometimes even replacing traditional hobbies.

title: P3 Discussion - Dining Culture and Festival Food
content: Is it common for students to dine with each other on school days in your country? Yes, of course. In our country, students often eat together on school days. The main reason is that we have a fixed schedule with regular meal times, so we always have meals with our classmates during lunch and dinner breaks. However, dining together doesn't just mean having food. It is also a great chance to share interesting things and discuss difficult problems that came up in class. What food do you eat on special occasions like the Spring Festival or the Mid-Autumn Festival? Well, let me take the Mid-Autumn Festival as an example. We always eat mooncakes at that time. The reason we eat this special food is that there is a mythological story about Chang'e flying to the moon. In addition, the festival is a symbol of reunion, so we always share mooncakes and admire the full moon with our family on that night.

title: Describe a great dinner - Grandpa's 70th birthday
content: Well, in my memory, I once enjoyed a great dinner at a five-star hotel. It was my grandpa's 70th birthday celebration. Before that, I had never set foot in such a luxurious hotel. Every time I passed by the five-star hotel, I sincerely wished I could walk in and experience it. Luckily, thanks to my grandpa's birthday, I eventually had the chance to dine there. The dinner party had 30 tables in total, and there were a lot of exquisite dishes such as white-cut pork, Australian beef, and deep-sea fish. In addition, they also served premium drinks like Maotai. To be honest, I had never been exposed to such luxurious things before. This dinner really broadened my horizons and gave me a special experience in my ordinary life. In the future, I will undoubtedly hold a wonderful dinner party for my family too when I have enough resources. It wasn't just a display of wealth — it was a completely new experience for me.

title: Describe a subject of science - Computer Science
content: Well, I'd like to talk about computer science, which I want to learn more about because I'm genuinely interested in it. Before I started learning computer science, the only way I interacted with a computer was playing video games, and I never imagined how a game or a website was actually built. However, when I entered university, I was truly fascinated by the world of computer science. As a result, I've learned advanced programming languages such as Python and Java. What's more, I've gained a clear understanding of how to build a website or a game from scratch. To be honest, I really want to dive deeper into this field, and my dream job is to be a programmer working at an internet company. In the future, I will continue to devote myself to learning computer science, regardless of whether I can fully achieve my dreams.

title: P3 Discussion - Children and Science Education
content: Why do some children not like learning science at school? Well, from my perspective, I think the main reason is that learning science requires a lot of patience. Students have to follow specific procedures and wait a long time to observe experimental results when conducting science experiments. By contrast, other subjects such as math or history can provide more immediate feedback after students invest their time. Should scientists explain the research process to the public? Yes, of course. I believe it is a necessary way to popularize science. For many people, they may never come into contact with science, much less understand the scientific process. So when scientists break down their research for non-experts, they not only share the details of their work but also help promote scientific literacy among the general public.

title: P3 Discussion - Saying Sorry in China
content: Do people in your country like to say sorry? Yes, of course. In our country, people always say sorry when they cause inconvenience to others. The most common situation is when people want to catch the subway or other public transport during rush hour. They run fast and push others aside, so they usually apologize to those around them at the same time. Why do some people refuse to say sorry to others? Well, from my perspective, I think the main reason is that they believe the other party is at fault. However, it doesn't mean those people are impolite. What they need is a fair justification. If the facts clearly demonstrate that it's their fault, they will sincerely offer an apology.

title: P3 Discussion - Shopping in Small Shops vs Online
content: Why do some people not like shopping in small shops? Well, in my opinion, I think those people are worried about the product quality. Generally speaking, if a shop is small, it may indicate that the owner doesn't have enough capital to expand the business. So, subconsciously, we tend to be skeptical about the quality of their products. What are the differences between online shopping and in-store shopping? Well, I think the biggest difference is the quality inspection process. For instance, we can check the quality of products firsthand when shopping in a physical store. In contrast, the quality of products cannot be guaranteed through online shopping, since we can only rely on pictures and reviews before making a purchase.
